Comparing feature sets with k-fold cross-validation improved precision from 71% to 87%. I also automated the collection of 8,000 executive email addresses for a joint BCG survey on team structure.

Using pandas and regex, I standardized athlete names, dates, divisions, and placements, and explored matching athletes across competitions to support longitudinal analysis.

copy.projects_intro: Things I’ve been working on, from raw data to something useful.
copy.ginseng_summary: Connecting merchandise sales, ticketing, and Instagram campaigns to reporting that supports everyday decisions.
copy.ginseng_problem: Merchandise orders, ticketing exports, and Instagram story links lived in separate places. Manual spreadsheet updates made it difficult to compare product performance, track campaign activity, and account for refunds arriving later.
copy.ginseng_approach: Python integrates Shopify API JSON responses, ticketing CSV exports, and tagged website activity. The project models 5,000+ customer, product, order, and refund records, with daily incremental ELT coordinated by Airflow. Validation, run logs, PostgreSQL UPSERT, and Snowflake MERGE support reliable retries; dbt SQL models prepare warehouse reporting data.
copy.ginseng_output: Power BI dashboards consolidate sales, customer, merchandise, refund, and ticket activity for business reporting. The interactive demo uses fictional data to show source normalization, duplicate handling, late refunds, and campaign reporting.
copy.photos_intro: Hiking, cooking, and places I’ve been.
copy.pitch_summary: Measuring how quickly soccer teams apply defensive pressure and regain possession after losing the ball. Evaluated on 35 annotated transitions, with a 0.7-second mean absolute timing error.
copy.pitch_details: I annotated 35 possession losses, then combined YOLOv8 player detection and tracking with OpenCV homography to map movement onto pitch coordinates. For each transition, I calculated pressure-response and possession-recovery times and compared automated event timing with manual annotations, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.7 seconds.
copy.datathon_summary: Finding unusual reporting patterns in 1M+ Los Angeles crime records. Our team flagged 3% of records for review and placed 4th in the datathon.
copy.datathon_details: I cleaned invalid entries and engineered reporting-delay features to examine irregular reporting patterns. We applied Local Outlier Factor and Isolation Forest to detect density-based and tree-based anomalies, flagging 3% of records for review. Those flags helped prioritize data-quality checks; they did not establish that a record was incorrect.

copy.project_summary: One reporting workflow for orders, payments, refunds, and ticket sales.
copy.problem: Sales activity lives across separate order, payment, refund, and ticket records. Reporting needs consistent definitions and a reliable way to bring those records together.
copy.approach: A Python ingestion process loads source records into a structured data model. Incremental loads feed Snowflake; dbt builds reporting tables, and Airflow coordinates each step.
copy.validation: Check unique keys, missing relationships, and invalid amounts. Reconcile totals back to the sources and rerun loads to confirm they do not duplicate sales.
